theory.intro: Displacement, velocity and acceleration are joined by calculus. Differentiating takes you from $x$ to $v$ to $a$; integrating takes you back the other way, using initial conditions to find each constant.
facts: Differentiating goes $x \to v \to a$, and integrating goes $a \to v \to x$.
Every integration introduces a constant, so one initial condition is needed for each constant.
The **displacement** of a particle over $t = p$ to $t = q$ is $x(q) - x(p)$, and it may be negative.
The **distance travelled** is the total length of path covered, so it is never negative.
The particle changes direction at a time where $v = 0$ and $v$ changes sign there.
If the particle changes direction inside an interval, split the interval at that time and add the distance of each leg.
A particle is **speeding up** when $v$ and $a$ have the same sign, and slowing down when their signs differ.
A positive acceleration alone does not mean speeding up: a particle with $v < 0$ and $a > 0$ is slowing down.
steps: Identify which of $x$, $v$ or $a$ is given, then differentiate or integrate to reach the one you need.
Use the given initial conditions to find the constant produced by each integration.
To find when the particle is at rest or changes direction, set $v = 0$ and solve for $t \ge 0$.
For distance travelled, split the interval at each time of rest and add the size of each change in displacement.

foundation.question_text: A particle has acceleration $a = 6t - 4\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and initial velocity $v(0) = 5\text{ m/s}$. Find $v$ as a function of $t$.
A particle has acceleration $a = 12t^{2} + 2\text{ m/s}^{2}$, and $v = 10\text{ m/s}$ when $t = 1$. Find $v$ as a function of $t$.
A particle has velocity $v = 3t^{2} - 8t\text{ m/s}$ and initial displacement $x(0) = 2\text{ m}$. Find $x$ as a function of $t$.
A particle has velocity $v = 4 - 2t\text{ m/s}$, and $x = 7\text{ m}$ when $t = 2$. Find $x$ as a function of $t$.
A particle has acceleration $a = 12t\text{ m/s}^{2}$, with $v(0) = -3\text{ m/s}$ and $x(0) = 1\text{ m}$. Find $x$ as a function of $t$.
foundation.solution_text:
$v = \displaystyle\int 12t\,dt$
$= 6t^{2} + c$
$\text{When } t = 0,\ v = -3:\ c = -3$
$v = 6t^{2} - 3$
$x = \displaystyle\int (6t^{2} - 3)\,dt$
$= 2t^{3} - 3t + d$
$\text{When } t = 0,\ x = 1:\ d = 1$
$x = 2t^{3} - 3t + 1$

foundation.question_text: A particle has displacement $x = t^{3} + 2t$ metres at time $t$ seconds. Find its displacement between $t = 1$ and $t = 3$.
A particle has velocity $v = 6t + 2\text{ m/s}$ for $t \ge 0$. Find its displacement over the first $4$ seconds.
At time $t = 2$ a particle has velocity $v = -5\text{ m/s}$ and acceleration $a = -3\text{ m/s}^{2}$. Is the particle speeding up or slowing down? Give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
$v = -5,\ a = -3$
$\text{Both are negative, so } v \text{ and } a \text{ have the same sign.}$
The particle is speeding up.

foundation.question_text: At time $t = 3$ a particle has velocity $v = 8\text{ m/s}$ and acceleration $a = -2\text{ m/s}^{2}$. Is the particle speeding up or slowing down? Give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
$v = 8,\ a = -2$
$\text{The signs are opposite, so the speed } |v| \text{ is decreasing.}$
The particle is slowing down.

development.question_text: A particle has acceleration $a = 6t - 10\text{ m/s}^{2}$, with $v(0) = 4\text{ m/s}$ and $x(0) = -2\text{ m}$. Find $v$ and $x$ as functions of $t$.
A particle moves with $x = t^{3} - 6t^{2} + 5$ metres for $t \ge 0$. Find the time at which the particle changes direction, and justify that the direction does change there.
development.solution_text:
$v = \dot{x} = 3t^{2} - 12t$
$\text{Set } v = 0:$
$3t(t - 4) = 0$
$t = 0\text{ or } t = 4$
$\text{For } 0 < t < 4,\ v < 0\text{ (e.g. } v(1) = -9)$
$\text{For } t > 4,\ v > 0\text{ (e.g. } v(5) = 15)$
The velocity changes sign at $t = 4$, so the particle changes direction at $t = 4$ seconds.

development.question_text: A particle moves with $x = t^{4} - 8t^{2}$ metres for $t \ge 0$. Find the time at which the particle changes direction.
development.solution_text:
$v = \dot{x} = 4t^{3} - 16t$
$\text{Set } v = 0:$
$4t(t - 2)(t + 2) = 0$
$t = 0,\ t = 2\text{ or } t = -2$
$\text{Since } t \ge 0,\ \text{the interior solution is } t = 2$
$v(1) = -12\text{ and } v(3) = 60$
The velocity changes sign at $t = 2$, so the particle changes direction at $t = 2$ seconds.

development.question_text: A particle moves with $x = t^{2} - 6t + 8$ metres for $0 \le t \le 5$ seconds. Find (a) its displacement over this interval and (b) the distance it travels over this interval.
A particle has velocity $v = 3t^{2} - 12\text{ m/s}$ and starts at the origin, $x(0) = 0$. Find the distance it travels in the first $3$ seconds.
A particle moves with $x = t^{3} - 2t^{2}$ metres for $3 \le t \le 5$ seconds. Find its displacement over this interval.
A particle moves with $x = t^{3} - 6t^{2} + 4t$ metres for $t \ge 0$. Is the particle speeding up or slowing down when $t = 3$? Give a reason.
development.solution_text:
$v = \dot{x} = 3t^{2} - 12t + 4$
$a = \ddot{x} = 6t - 12$
$v(3) = 27 - 36 + 4$
$= -5\text{ m/s}$
$a(3) = 18 - 12$
$= 6\text{ m/s}^{2}$
$\text{The signs are opposite, so the speed } |v| \text{ is decreasing.}$
The particle is slowing down, even though the acceleration is positive.

development.question_text:
The velocity–time graph of a particle moving in a straight line is shown, where $v = t^{2} - 6t + 8\text{ m/s}$ for $0 \le t \le 6$ seconds.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$t$ (s)}, ylabel={$v$ (m/s)},
             xmin=-0.6, xmax=6.8, ymin=-3, ymax=9.5,
             xtick={1,2,3,4,5,6}, ytick={-2,2,4,6,8}, samples=100, clip=false,
             width=10cm, height=8cm]
\addplot[thick, domain=0:6] {x*x - 6*x + 8};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
State the times at which the particle is at rest, and the interval during which it moves in the negative direction.
development.solution_text:
$\text{At rest where } v = 0:$
$t^{2} - 6t + 8 = 0$
$(t - 2)(t - 4) = 0$
$t = 2\text{ s and } t = 4\text{ s}$
$\text{The graph is below the } t\text{-axis between these times.}$
The particle moves in the negative direction for $2 < t < 4$.

development.question_text:
The displacement–time graph of a particle moving in a straight line is shown, where $x = 4t - t^{2}$ metres for $0 \le t \le 5$ seconds.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$t$ (s)}, ylabel={$x$ (m)},
             xmin=-0.6, xmax=5.8, ymin=-6.5, ymax=5.5,
             xtick={1,2,3,4,5}, ytick={-6,-4,-2,2,4}, samples=100, clip=false,
             width=10cm, height=8cm]
\addplot[thick, domain=0:5] {4*x - x*x};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Find the time at which the particle is at rest, and explain why this is not the same as the time it is at the origin.
development.solution_text:
$v = \dot{x} = 4 - 2t$
$\text{At rest, } v = 0:$
$4 - 2t = 0$
$t = 2\text{ s}$
$x(2) = 8 - 4$
$= 4\text{ m}$
$\text{At the origin, } x = 0:$
$t(4 - t) = 0$
$t = 0\text{ s and } t = 4\text{ s}$
At rest means the velocity is zero, which happens at the turning point $t = 2$ where the particle is $4$ m from the origin; the particle is at the origin at $t = 0$ and $t = 4$, where it is moving.

development.question_text: A particle has acceleration $a = 6\cos 3t\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and initial velocity $v(0) = 2\text{ m/s}$. Find $v$ as a function of $t$.

mastery.question_text: A particle has acceleration $a = 6t - 24\text{ m/s}^{2}$, with $v(0) = 36\text{ m/s}$ and $x(0) = 0\text{ m}$. Find the distance travelled by the particle in the first $7$ seconds.
A particle moves with $x = t^{3} - 9t^{2} + 15t + 2$ metres for $0 \le t \le 6$ seconds. Find every interval on which the particle is speeding up.
mastery.solution_text:
$v = \dot{x} = 3t^{2} - 18t + 15$
$= 3(t - 1)(t - 5)$
$a = \ddot{x} = 6t - 18$
$v = 0\text{ at } t = 1,\ t = 5;\ a = 0\text{ at } t = 3$
$\text{On } 0 < t < 1:\ v > 0,\ a < 0$
$\text{On } 1 < t < 3:\ v < 0,\ a < 0$
$\text{On } 3 < t < 5:\ v < 0,\ a > 0$
$\text{On } 5 < t < 6:\ v > 0,\ a > 0$
The signs of $v$ and $a$ agree on $1 < t < 3$ and on $5 < t < 6$, so the particle is speeding up on those intervals.

mastery.question_text: A particle has acceleration $a = 12t - 6\text{ m/s}^{2}$. It is at $x = 4\text{ m}$ when $t = 0$ and at $x = 5\text{ m}$ when $t = 1$. Find $x$ as a function of $t$.
A particle moves with $x = te^{-t}$ metres for $t \ge 0$. Show that the particle changes direction exactly once, and find its displacement at that time.
mastery.solution_text:
$v = \dot{x} = e^{-t} - te^{-t}$
$= (1 - t)e^{-t}$
$\text{Since } e^{-t} > 0,\ v = 0\text{ only when } t = 1$
$\text{For } 0 \le t < 1,\ v > 0;\ \text{for } t > 1,\ v < 0$
$\text{The velocity changes sign once, at } t = 1\text{ s.}$
$x(1) = 1 \times e^{-1}$
$= e^{-1}\text{ m}$
